title: Cell Structure
subject: Biology
description: Organelles of animal, plant and bacterial cells, plus the magnification formula.
author: StudyDeck sample

cards.back: Contains the cell's genetic material (DNA) and controls the cell's activities.
Controls which substances enter and leave the cell. It is partially permeable.
Jelly-like substance where most of the cell's chemical reactions happen.
Site of aerobic respiration, which releases energy for the cell.
cards.hint: Often called the powerhouse of the cell.

cards.back: Made of cellulose in plant cells. It strengthens and supports the cell.
Contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis.
Filled with cell sap. It helps keep the plant cell rigid.
A cell with no nucleus. Its DNA is free in the cytoplasm (e.g. bacteria).
A small ring of DNA found in bacterial (prokaryotic) cells.
A cell whose DNA is inside a nucleus (e.g. animal and plant cells).

cards.hint: Make sure both sizes are in the same units.

questions.question: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration, releasing energy for the cell.

questions.question: Which structures are found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
options: Cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole
questions.explanation: Animal and plant cells share the nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane, mitochondria and ribosomes. Only plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole.

questions.question: Where is the DNA found in a prokaryotic cell?
options: Free in the cytoplasm, with some in plasmids
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes have no nucleus. Their DNA is a single loop in the cytoplasm, plus small rings called plasmids.

questions.question: What is the cell wall of a plant cell made of?
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose. (Fungal cell walls are made of chitin.)

questions.question: An image is 5 mm long and the real object is 0.05 mm long. What is the magnification?
What is the function of ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes join amino acids together to make proteins.
